catalog_entry.label: Tournament aggregate and match-event count props
contract_types: World Cup Matches to go to Penalties
World Cup Winner to Trail in a Match
World Cup Every Team to Score a Goal
catalog_entry.target: A count, sum or extreme of goals or match events aggregated across many matches in a tournament, relative to a strike or condition.
catalog_entry.mechanism: These markets settle on a count or extreme drawn from the 104-match tournament: total goals, the single highest score, how many ties go to penalties, how long the longest shootout lasts, whether the eventual winner ever trails, and whether every team scores. The outcome is generated by a goal-environment level for international football, the mismatch mix of the draw, the knockout structure that creates shootouts, and shared tournament-wide factors that make matches correlated; it is not a single-match total or a player race.

inputs.why: The level of goals per match times match count sets strikes for tournament and group-stage totals.
Shared tournament effects widen the totals distribution beyond independent matches.
Governs the longest-shootout and matches-to-penalties contracts.
Mismatch mix of the fixture list changes goals, blanks and comeback events.
Match-level goal count distribution is the building block of every aggregate here.
Tail dispersion of match totals drives the highest-scoring-game strike.
Probability a knockout tie reaches penalties determines the penalties count.
Team shootout skill alters whether a tie ends early or goes to sudden death.
Sets which side concedes first for Concede First type contracts.
Drives probability a team that falls behind recovers, which feeds Winner to Trail.
Zero-inflation per team governs Every Team to Score a Goal.
Defines which matches and goals count (group stage, extra time, own goals).
Rules wording needed for every series because none was sampled.

interactions.hypothesis: A group stage with more lopsided fixtures raises both total goals and the chance of one match with very many goals, because mismatch fattens the right tail of scoring.
A shared tournament effect shifts every match together, so the variance of tournament goals is larger than the independent sum and tail strikes are underpriced if matches are treated as independent.
The longest shootout is the maximum over a random number of shootouts, so the draw count and the sudden-death chance interact to set the extreme.

contract.settlement_definition: None of the nine series has sampled rules text (all NO_LISTING, titles only), so settlement is unverified. Titles imply counts or extremes over World Cup matches: 'World Cup Tournament Goals', 'World Cup Group Stage Goals', 'World Cup Team Goals', 'World Cup Highest Scoring Game', 'World Cup Matches to go to Penalties', 'World Cup Longest Penalty Shootout', 'World Cup Winner to Trail in a Match', 'World Cup Every Team to Score a Goal', 'World Cup Concede First'. Whether extra-time goals, shootout kicks and own goals count is not visible.
variants_and_edge_cases: Extra-time goals: a tournament goals count may include or exclude extra time; shootout kicks are normally not goals but a contract could say otherwise, and the sampled texts do not state it.
'World Cup Team Goals' may be a single-team tournament total or a single-match team total; the pack's reviewer notes the ambiguity and the title does not resolve it.
'Winner to Trail in a Match' could mean the tournament winner trails at any point in any of its matches, or any match winner that trailed; the two have very different probabilities.
'Concede First' is unclear on whether it is a count of teams, the identity of a team, or a match question about conceding first; no strike construction is visible.
'Longest Penalty Shootout' could be measured in rounds, kicks or total goals; ties between shootouts of equal length are not described.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated; likely FIFA official match reports and results as tracked by Kalshi's data provider, but the sampled rules are absent, so this is an assumption.

mechanism.summary: Each market is a function of the same 104 matches but picks a different statistic: a sum (tournament and group goals), a maximum (highest score, longest shootout), a count of rare events (penalties, trailing winners), or an all-teams conjunction (every team scores). The sum is governed by the goal level of international football and the mismatch mix of the draw. The maximum depends on the tail of the single-match score distribution. Shootout counts depend on knockout structure and on how often ties are level after extra time. The conjunction depends on the weakest attacks' blank rates in few matches. A shared tournament factor correlates all matches, widening every distribution beyond what independent matches would give, and the contract definitions change which goals and matches enter the statistic.

stages.name: Goal level of the tournament
stages.description: Goals per match average about 2.6 to 2.7 over recent World Cups, with group stage typically a bit higher than knockout where caution rises. The 2026 field has 48 teams so more weak-versus-strong fixtures; tournaments also differ by added-time and refereeing directives. The tournament mean is therefore estimated from team ratings and the draw, then shrunk toward historical values, producing the base rate for sums and for every match-level event.
stages.distribution: Match goals are overdispersed counts; the tournament mean is a latent level with between-tournament variance beyond Poisson.

stages.name: Mismatch mix and shared shocks
stages.description: The draw fixes who plays whom in the 72 group games, and the bracket then adds lopsided or balanced knockout games. Lopsided fixtures raise totals and the chance of a single high-scoring match; shared factors such as heat, travel distance across three host countries or an officiating directive move all matches together. This stage turns independent match rates into correlated tournament outcomes.
stages.distribution: Mixture over gap buckets plus a common random effect; heavy right tail of a single match score driven by mismatches.

stages.name: Knockout draws, extra time and shootouts
stages.description: From the round of 32 onward a level match goes to extra time and then penalties. The count of shootouts is a binomial-type count over about 32 knockout matches with a draw-after-extra-time probability near a few percent each, and each shootout length is a stopping time of kick conversions. The longest shootout is the maximum over a random number of such stopping times, so the count and the sudden-death chance both matter.
stages.distribution: Count of shootouts is small and discrete; shootout length is a right-skewed stopping time with a long tail; the maximum is an extreme-value quantity.

stages.name: In-match event sequences
stages.description: Concede First, Winner to Trail and Every Team to Score depend on within-match order of goals and on blank rates. The eventual winner trails if it concedes first and then recovers, which depends on first-goal hazard and the response of the trailing team. A team failing to score through its group matches and any knockouts removes it from the every-team-scores set, with excess blank rates for weak attacks dominating.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli events per team-match with zero-inflation for weak attacks; conjunctions over many teams are dominated by a few low-probability members.

stages.name: Contract scope and counting rules
stages.description: The statistic depends on which matches and which goals count: group stage only or all, extra time goals, own goals, shootout kicks, and whether matches abandoned or replayed are counted. The sampled series have no rules text, so each variant is a distinct random variable and the model must carry the scope flag rather than assume one reading.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the rules; differences between readings are shifts of a few goals in totals and a different extremal definition for the longest shootout.

talent_strength.note: Team ratings enter through the goal level and draw composition.

role_personnel.note: Dependence on a focal striker explains blank rates for weak attacks.

availability_news.note: Individual injuries shift a team's goal rate slightly and are absorbed into pre-tournament ratings; for tournament-wide counts the effect averages out over 48 teams and is second-order to the goal level and format.

coaching_scheme.note: Cautious knockout play and chasing behaviour.

environment.note: Heat, altitude and travel across hosts act as shared shocks.

game_context_script.note: Score order and level ties drive events.

pace_volume.note: Matches played and chances per match set the count.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Dead rubbers and must-win third group matches.

settlement_contract.note: Scope flags; no rules text sampled.

soc.tournament_goal_environment.label: Tournament goals-per-match environment from past World Cups and tournament-specific drivers
soc.tournament_goal_environment.mechanism: Expected goals per match across a whole tournament, set by the mix of strong and weak teams, the group format and rule directives such as added time and VAR.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.rationale: Total goals is a sum of 104 correlated matches, so the level matters more than any one team. Past World Cups sit around 2.6 to 2.7 goals per match but a 48-team field adds more lopsided group games, and a longer-added-time directive raises totals. A model built from club league averages misses the tournament-specific level.
soc.tournament_goal_environment.measurement: For each World Cup since 1998: goals per 90 minutes split by group stage and knockout, by gap in team strength bucket, and by added-time directive era. Fit a Poisson-gamma mixture across matches; set the 2026 mean from team ratings of the actual field via the group draw, shrunk to the historical mean with k=3 tournaments. As-of = after the draw is fixed; update after each round.
free_sources: FIFA match reports and historical results datasets (free)
raw_data: match-level goals by stage and tournament
soc.tournament_goal_environment.why: Settles Tournament Goals, Group Stage Goals and Team Goals strikes, which are functions of this level times the match count.

soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.label: Shared tournament-wide factor affecting all matches' scoring
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.mechanism: Common causes that move every match together: ball, climate, officiating directives, travel burden and a low-scoring or high-scoring tournament style.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.rationale: Match outcomes within a tournament are not independent: one referee directive on penalties or a heat wave across venues shifts the whole distribution. Ignoring this makes the variance of totals and counts too narrow, which matters most for tail strikes such as a record goals total.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.measurement: Estimate the between-tournament variance of per-match goals residual after team strength, using World Cups and continental finals since 2000 (random effect per tournament); report the intraclass correlation and its posterior. Use the implied standard deviation as the dispersion widening for tournament sums. As-of = pre-tournament; update only with documented directive changes.
soc.tournament_common_shock_factor.why: Governs how wide the distribution of tournament totals and event counts is beyond independent-match noise.

soc.shootout_length_distribution.label: Penalty shootout length and per-kick conversion distribution
soc.shootout_length_distribution.mechanism: A shootout lasts five rounds each unless decided early, then sudden death; its length is a stopping-time of kick conversions.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.rationale: The longest shootout is an extreme of a small number of events, so it depends on how many shootouts occur and on the chance of each reaching sudden death. Conversion near three quarters per kick implies early finishes are common but a long run of equal outcomes occurs rarely.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.measurement: From all World Cup and continental shootouts since 1982 (about 40), compute per-kick conversion with beta shrinkage (prior mean 0.75, strength 20 kicks), P(shootout reaches kick 11), and P(length>=k) via the stopping rule; combine with the expected number of shootouts to give the distribution of the maximum. As-of = bracket known.
soc.shootout_length_distribution.why: Directly specifies the Longest Penalty Shootout contract and feeds the matches-to-penalties count.

soc.group_gap_composition.label: Distribution of strength gaps across scheduled group and knockout matches
soc.group_gap_composition.mechanism: The tournament's schedule fixes a list of pairings whose strength gaps determine how many lopsided and how many balanced matches occur.
soc.group_gap_composition.rationale: Goal totals and trailing events depend on gap: lopsided matches produce more goals and fewer comebacks, balanced ones more draws and shootouts. A 48-team field has more lopsided group games than 32 teams, so past World Cup rates cannot be applied unadjusted.
soc.group_gap_composition.measurement: Using pre-tournament team ratings and the final draw, compute for each of the 72 group matches the rating gap and the implied goal expectations; bucket into quintiles and compare with past World Cups' bucket frequencies. As-of = after the draw.
soc.group_gap_composition.why: Moves group-stage goals and every-team-scores events by changing the mix of mismatch fixtures.

soc.goal_dist.reason: The match goal distribution is the unit that is summed or maximised; must be taken from international matches, not club leagues, and from regulation time only if the rules say so.

soc.total_goal_tail_dispersion.reason: Highest Scoring Game is an extreme of 104 match totals, so tail dispersion by mismatch bucket is the quantity that sets the strike.

soc.extra_time_shootout_model.reason: Matches to go to Penalties and Longest Penalty Shootout depend on the chance each knockout tie reaches a shootout; needs a national-team calibration.

soc.penalty_shootout_skill.reason: Skill differences are small relative to the noise of a shootout, so this only slightly shifts length and count; kept as context.

soc.first_goal_hazard.reason: Concede First and Winner to Trail both turn on who scores first; timing matters less than identity, so secondary.

soc.trailing_team_response_hazard.reason: Determines whether a team behind comes back, the mechanism behind Winner to Trail in a Match; mostly estimated from club data and needs national-team caution.

soc.team_fail_to_score_propensity.reason: Every Team to Score a Goal is a conjunction across 48 teams, so a few teams with excess blank rates dominate the probability.

soc.competition_scope_and_win_definition.reason: Scope flags decide whether extra-time goals, shootout kicks and own goals are counted, and every series here is unverified.

m.rules_text.reason: None of the nine series has rules text sampled; the wording defines what is counted and must be obtained first.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of a 7-goal or higher match rises convexly with the strength gap, so a draw with several extreme mismatches lifts the Highest Scoring Game probability much more than the same average gap spread evenly.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated highest-score distributions from the real fixture gaps against fixtures with the same mean gap but equalised.

interactions.mechanism: A tournament-level random effect makes total goals a mixture, so the upper and lower tails of tournament totals are fatter than a sum of independent matches; strikes far from the mean are most affected.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the tournament random-effect variance from past World Cups and compare tail probabilities with and without it.

interactions.mechanism: The longest shootout exists only if at least one tie reaches penalties, and longer ones need sudden death; conditional on few shootouts occurring the maximum is short with high probability, so count and length must be modelled jointly.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the knockout bracket and shootout lengths jointly and compare the maximum with a model using an average count.

interactions.mechanism: A team can only 'trail' if the opponent scores first, and recovery depends on how the trailing team responds; the two hazards together set P(winner conceded first) which is far from the product of marginal rates for a favourite facing a low block.
interactions.how_to_test: Split matches by favourite status and compare observed rate of winners who trailed with the product of marginal first-goal and recovery rates.

interactions.mechanism: A weak team that already needs a goal in its last group game raises attacking intent and its scoring chance; one already eliminated may not, so blank rates differ across the group-stage rounds and the 'every team scores' conjunction is sensitive to round-three incentives.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team blank rates in round-three group matches by stakes bucket against rounds one and two.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear mean effect on sums but convex effect on tail probabilities of a record total
nonlinearities.why: Totals respond linearly to the mean goal level, but the probability of exceeding a high strike changes much faster than the mean because the tail of an overdispersed count is steep.

nonlinearities.shape: Geometric decay after round five in the sudden-death phase
nonlinearities.why: Each additional sudden-death round occurs with probability near one half squared plus the complement, so length decays geometrically; this makes the longest shootout a thin-tailed quantity compared with total goals.

nonlinearities.shape: Conjunction across 48 teams: one weak team's blank probability dominates
nonlinearities.why: The probability that every team scores is a product over many teams, so a few teams with low scoring probability and excess zero rates lower the product disproportionately.

catalog_entry.label: Tournament match composition and venue
catalog_entry.target: Which teams, player or venue appear in a specified tournament match, set by bracket progression and the published schedule.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The occupants and venue of a numbered tournament match come from structure plus results: the schedule fixes the stadium and date of each match number, group finishing positions and the cross-group ranking of third-placed teams map to knockout slots through a fixed table, and each slot is filled by simulated results. A player appears only if his team reaches the match and he is available and selected. The mechanism is bracket plumbing, not the match result or the tournament winner.

inputs.why: Maps group position to match slot, date and venue; the structural core of every contract here.
Provides the probabilities of each team occupying each slot, including the third-place cross-group effect.
Determines whether a named player is eligible for a given match.
Match simulation underlies group results and knockout advancement.
Gives the opponent set and path conditional on finishing rank.
Path difficulty indicates how likely a team is to survive to a stated round.
Group tie-breaks decide ranks and third-place ordering.
Remaining group permutations determine who qualifies and in what slot.
Single-leg knockout advancement including extra time and penalties.
Injury status decides whether a named player can appear.
Minutes expectation separates starting players from squad players for appearance questions.
Postponement or relocation risk can change the game location.
Team strengths feed match results that fill the bracket.
Wording defines whether location means stadium or city and what counts as playing.

interactions.hypothesis: Venue and opponent depend on which third-place groups qualify, so the slot assignment is a joint function across groups and cannot be obtained from marginal group probabilities.
Close group tables resolve on tie-break order, so the probability of a team taking a slot is sensitive to how goal difference and head-to-head are ordered.
A player contract needs the team to arrive, eligibility, and selection; a card ban or rotation can remove a starter even if the team progresses.

contract.settlement_definition: No rules text sampled for KXWCTEAMSINGAME ('World Cup Teams in Game'), KXWCLOCATION ('World Cup Game Location') or KXWCPLAY ('World Cup Play in Game'); all NO_LISTING with titles only. They appear to settle on the teams, venue or a participant of a specific match, but the match referenced, the definition of location (stadium, city or country) and what counts as playing (in squad, in lineup, minutes) are not visible.
variants_and_edge_cases: Location could be stadium, city or host country; a venue switch for security, weather or scheduling would resolve differently under each.
'Play in Game' might mean appearing for any minutes, starting, or being in the matchday squad; a bench non-use would resolve differently.
'Teams in Game' could ask for an exact pairing in either order or for a team being one of the two; ordering and neutral-venue home labelling are unknown.
A match that is abandoned, replayed or relocated might void or settle on later facts; the sampled series give no text.
If the question is about a match whose slot depends on a third-place assignment table, the resolution depends on FIFA publishing the final bracket, with no stated fallback.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated; likely FIFA's official match schedule and match reports, but rules text is absent so this is assumed.

mechanism.summary: A numbered tournament match has a fixed date and stadium; who plays there comes from the bracket. Group results sort teams into positions; the best third-placed teams are chosen by a cross-group ranking and then assigned to slots through a lookup table keyed to which groups they come from. Knockout winners advance to the next fixed slot, so the later venues follow from the path. A named player appears only if his team reaches the match and he is eligible and chosen. The probability for any contract is therefore the sum over group outcomes through the slot mapping, with the schedule and regulation text defining the mapping, not a model of the match result itself.

stages.name: Fixed schedule and slot mapping
stages.description: The regulations pre-assign each match number a date, city and stadium and define which group positions feed which round-of-32 slot, and which slot each later winner enters. Host nations are typically placed so their group matches are at home and the bracket keeps them in home regions if they finish in certain positions, which makes venue depend on their group finish. This stage has no randomness but contains rule detail where errors are costly.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from group position to match number; the only uncertainty is whether amendments to the schedule occur.

stages.name: Group finishing and third-place ranking
stages.description: Each group's four teams play three matches and are sorted by tie-break order. The third-placed teams across all twelve groups are ranked on points, goal difference and goals scored, and the best eight advance. Which eight and from which groups sets their slots through the allocation table. Small points and goal-difference gaps decide the cut, making this stage highly sensitive to match results in the last round.
stages.distribution: Joint discrete distribution over group orderings; third-place cut driven by goal difference, with many ties at equal points broken by secondary criteria.

stages.name: Knockout advancement to the target match
stages.description: A team reaches a later numbered match only by winning each earlier tie, which may be settled in extra time or penalties. Teams whose path sends them through weak opponents have a higher chance to reach a specific slot; slot probability is a product over rounds conditioned on earlier results. Path difficulty and shootout resolution therefore enter.
stages.distribution: Product of Bernoulli advancement events with draw-resolution randomness; path correlation across teams because opponents are shared.

stages.name: Player eligibility and selection
stages.description: For a named-player contract, the team must reach the match; the player must not be suspended through red cards or accumulated yellows, must not be injured, and must be selected and used. Rotation in dead rubbers and managers' choices determine who plays, and the card reset point in the regulations decides who carries suspension forward.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with probability depending on a ban (known after the previous round), injury hazard and selection; mixture of near-certain starters and rotation players.

talent_strength.note: Match probabilities fill group tables and knockout slots.

opponent_matchup.note: Who a team meets depends on its slot.

role_personnel.note: Starter versus rotation status for player contracts.

availability_news.note: Injury and card bans determine player eligibility.

coaching_scheme.note: Tactics shape match results already represented by team strength, and bracket composition depends on results and fixed structure rather than on in-game scheme; only rotation matters, covered under player minutes.

environment.note: Venue and city are fixed per match number; location contracts are structural.

game_context_script.note: Extra time and shootouts decide who advances.

pace_volume.note: The outcome is which entity occupies a slot rather than a count of events or opportunities, so no pace or volume input applies to the composition and venue mechanism of these contracts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion rates affect the results that fill slots only through match probabilities already captured by team ratings; there is no per-opportunity rate in the contract itself that needs separate treatment.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Final-round stakes and rotation in groups.

officiating_rules.note: Tie-break order decides ranks and third-place cut.

settlement_contract.note: Definitions of location and play; no rules text sampled.

soc.bracket_slot_graph.label: Official tournament match graph: slots, match numbers, venues and third-place allocation
soc.bracket_slot_graph.mechanism: The published schedule fixes which slot plays which, in what stadium and on what date; entrants to each knockout slot come from group finishing positions through a fixed mapping.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.rationale: Teams in a game and the location are determined by structure plus results: a winner of group A plays the runner-up of group B in a named city, and the eight best third-place teams are assigned to slots by a lookup depending on which groups they come from. A single wrong cell in the lookup changes the venue. The allocation can differ from past World Cups, so it must be read from the regulations.
soc.bracket_slot_graph.measurement: Transcribe the regulation's match list into a directed graph: nodes are match numbers with date, city and stadium; edges map group position (1st, 2nd, best 3rd by combination) to slot. Encode the third-place table as a function of the set of qualifying third-place groups and validate that every combination yields a legal bracket. Test by checking against the official bracket for a hypothetical result. As-of = regulations publication; re-fetch if amended.
free_sources: FIFA competition regulations and match schedule (free)
raw_data: match schedule with numbers and venues
soc.bracket_slot_graph.why: These markets resolve on which teams or which venue appear in a numbered match, which the graph maps exactly.

soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of group finishing positions across all groups
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.mechanism: Simulated finishing order in each group, including the cross-group ranking of third-placed teams by points, goal difference and goals scored.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.rationale: Which team lands in a knockout slot depends on not just its own group but on the other groups through the best-thirds ranking. The cross-group coupling makes marginal group probabilities insufficient: the combination of third-place qualifiers decides slot assignment and so venue.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.measurement: Simulate all group games with the team goal model, apply the group tie-break order from the regulations (verify: points, then head-to-head, then goal difference, then goals scored, then fair play and rank), compute the third-place table across groups, and output the joint distribution of slot occupants for each knockout match as a team-by-match probability matrix. 20000 draws minimum. As-of = last completed match.
soc.group_rank_joint_distribution.why: Directly yields P(team in match) and P(venue) given the bracket mapping.

soc.suspension_accumulation_state.label: Card accumulation and suspension state of named players
soc.suspension_accumulation_state.mechanism: Players miss a match through red cards and accumulated yellow cards, with the count reset at a stated stage.
soc.suspension_accumulation_state.rationale: A 'Play in Game' contract for a player requires the team to reach the match and the player to be eligible and selected. Yellow-card totals carry between rounds until a reset, so a player one card from a ban is at risk of missing a knockout tie. Suspensions are known only after the previous round.
soc.suspension_accumulation_state.measurement: For each player: yellow count, red cards, and reset round from the regulations; probability of a ban = P(card in next match) given prior cards and referee card rate, with shrinkage k=20 matches; combine with selection probability from minutes history. As-of = disciplinary list published after each match.
soc.suspension_accumulation_state.why: A player question is lost to a ban even if the team progresses; this is the only suspension-based pathway.

soc.comp_sim.reason: Group and knockout simulation is the engine, but it must output slot occupancy and venue rather than just title or advancement probabilities.

soc.seeded_bracket_path_given_finish.reason: Written for UEFA league-phase seeding; the concept transfers to this bracket but the mapping must be reimplemented from the World Cup regulations.

soc.bracket_path_difficulty.reason: Helps estimate survival to later rounds, but the contract here is about presence in a slot, not winning the tournament.

soc.tiebreaker_rules.reason: Order of group tie-breaks and the third-place ranking criteria decide slots; wrong order gives wrong venue.

soc.group_stage_scenarios.reason: Useful during the group stage for enumerating outcomes; becomes irrelevant once groups are final.

soc.tie_advancement_state_tree.reason: Single-leg knockouts only need regulation, extra time and shootout; the two-leg part of the tree is not applicable.

soc.injuries.reason: Matters only for the player-appearance contract and for a team's advancement; low weight for team and venue contracts.

soc.player_minutes_expectation.reason: Separates starters from rotation players when a contract asks if a named player plays.

soc.abandonment_risk.reason: Relocation or abandonment is rare at a World Cup but would change location; context only.

soc.ratings.reason: Provides the match probabilities that fill slots; uncertainty must propagate to bracket composition.

m.rules_text.reason: No rules text is sampled; definitions of location, 'play' and 'teams in game' must be read.

interactions.mechanism: A third-placed team's slot depends on which other groups also produce a qualifying third, so P(team plays in a given city) is a sum over joint third-place combinations rather than a function of its own group; marginal probabilities misassign venue.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare venue probabilities from the joint simulation with those from independent group marginals pushed through the mapping.

interactions.mechanism: When two teams level on points are separated by a lower-level tie-break, the group position flips at a hard threshold, so small changes in goal difference move a team from one slot to another; the probability is a step in goal difference at equal points.
interactions.how_to_test: Re-simulate with the tie-break order permuted and count the slot assignments that change.

interactions.mechanism: Eligibility is a gate: a player one yellow from a ban has the same selection probability only if not suspended, so appearance probability is selection times the gate, and the gate is known after the preceding match.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare appearance rates for players with versus without a suspension risk, controlling for starter status.

interactions.mechanism: Reaching a late slot requires winning every earlier tie, so probability multiplies across rounds; small per-round differences from path difficulty compound for deep slots.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute reach probability for later slots from the round-by-round product and compare with a single-step win estimate.

interactions.mechanism: Under normal conditions the venue is fixed by match number; a relocation regime triggered by security, weather or an administrative change replaces the mapping, so location contracts are mixtures of a near-certain base state and a small switch state.
interactions.how_to_test: Review past tournaments for venue changes and fit the switch probability per host region.

nonlinearities.shape: Step change at the best-eight third-place cut
nonlinearities.why: Only eight of twelve third-placed teams advance, so qualification is a hard cut on a cross-group ranking; a small change in goal difference moves a team from certain exit to a full knockout slot.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at the card count that triggers a ban
nonlinearities.why: A ban applies discretely at the accumulation threshold, so the risk to a player jumps when he is on the card count just below it and falls to zero after the stated reset.
